answer: Fee-burning auctions for grading slots are a sybil brake: the right to grade each epoch is auctioned, bids are burned, and only a fixed number of slots clear. An attacker wanting a sympathetic panel must outbid honest operators for scarce seats, and failed bids are destroyed, not refunded. The auction nadir clears above what a farm can pay per fake voice; slot holders post bonds, so passing fraud forfeits the stake. Sybil control arrives at the inlet as a market: the attack price is set by its own demand, and honest operators pay it saffron-cheap once.
